title: Gin Tama
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In an alternate Edo-era Japan conquered by aliens called Amanto, swords are banned and the samurai class has collapsed. Former rebel samurai Gintoki Sakata runs an odd-jobs business, the Yorozuya, with teenager Shinpachi and the super-strong alien girl Kagura. Mostly episodic parody and gag comedy alternates with long serious arcs about old comrades, coups and an immortal villain.
life_message: It holds up keeping your own soul straight and protecting the people in arm's reach, whatever the rulers say.

content.note: Sword fights, war flashbacks and character deaths in serious arcs (Wikipedia plot; AniList War, Swordplay, Tragedy).
Tragic backstories and an apocalyptic final arc against Utsuro (Wikipedia; AniList Tragedy).
Frequent crude sexual gags, a Yoshiwara red-light district arc (Wikipedia notes many penis jokes; MangaDex suggestive).
Rude, insulting banter typical of gag manga (to verify).
Gintoki's drinking and Hijikata's chain-smoking played for laughs (to verify).
Survivor guilt from the war shapes Gintoki and his comrades (to verify).
Toilet humor, slacking and swordplay; heroes defy police and government (to verify).
Heavy parody of other Jump series and brands; meta jokes about sales (Wikipedia).

dominant: Found-family loyalty; absurdist parody; a personal samurai code

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Gintoki fights to keep his 'soul' straight and answers threats to friends personally, not through courts.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Heroes ignore the sword ban and laugh at the puppet shogunate; freedom from rules is celebrated.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty runs to the Yorozuya found family and old comrades before the state.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rank is mocked, though reverence for the teacher Shouyou anchors the story.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Samurai spirit honored while religion and custom are freely parodied.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Eccentric self-expression and tolerance of oddballs over thrift; Gintoki is a broke slacker.

folkways.japan: The samurai code (bushido), senpai-teacher bonds and Edo nostalgia are Japanese cultural material that the series both honors and parodies.

delivery.evidence: Loyalty themes surface in serious arcs between gag chapters; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: A personal code of loyalty is carried by Gintoki's actions amid parody, per summaries.

winners_losers: Misfits who keep their loyalties win; corrupt officials and nihilistic former comrades lose. Sympathy goes to a scruffy, anti-authority loyalty.
